title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Forward Collision Avoidance complaint cluster
summary: 21 complaints cluster around collision, braking, brake, forward collision, forward, cherokee. Status: EMERGING.

claims.text: Owners of 2015-2025 JEEP GRAND CHEROKEE describe a recurring forward collision avoidance problem (collision, braking, brake, forward collision, forward, cherokee).
Some reports involve a crash, fire or injury.
The most similar past recall (24V125000, LEXUS, TOYOTA) concerned: Unexpected vehicle movement may occur when the vehicle is in neutral and the brakes are not applied.
A related manufacturer bulletin exists: Auto Emergency Braking (AEB) Unavailable – Service Required Message In Cluster

recommended_action: Analyst review of the cited complaints; consider a preliminary evaluation.

R-24V125000.text: Unexpected vehicle movement may occur when the vehicle is in neutral and the brakes are not applied.
R-24V125000.consequence: Unexpected vehicle movement can increase the risk of a crash.

R-19V561000.text: Due to a problem with the front brake master cylinder, the front brakes may drag or apply, causing the motorcycle to unexpectedly slow down or stop completely without activating the rear brake light.
R-19V561000.consequence: Unexpectedly slowing down or stopping while driving with no warning to following traffic can increase the risk of a crash.

R-24V349000.text: The brakes may activate suddenly due to the automatic braking system falsely detecting certain objects while driving.
R-24V349000.consequence: Unexpected braking increases the risk of a crash.

R-19V907000.text: The Smart Brake System (SBS) can falsely detect an obstacle while driving, activating the automatic emergency braking system and suddenly stopping the vehicle.
R-19V907000.consequence: Stopping the vehicle unexpectedly increases the risk of a crash.

R-16V240000.text: The affected vehicles, equipped with an eight-speed automatic transmission and a monostable gear selector, may not adequately warn the driver when driver's door is opened and the vehicle is not in PARK, allowing them to exit the vehicle while the vehicle is still in gear.

R-24V838000.text: A malfunction in the antilock-brake system (ABS) module may incorrectly illuminate the brake lights and disable the ABS and electronic stability control (ESC).  In addition, the vehicle operator may be able to start and shift out of Park without the brake pedal being applied.

R-15V469000.text: The affected vehicles may be equipped with rear lower control arms that may have been incorrectly heat treated. This may cause the rear lower control arm to fracture.
